The sizes are workable, and my arithmetic check caught a bug before anything was saved. The `D` check printed 1.81 rather than 1.0, because I built `c` with `gq²` when the optimal form, and the one my scale formula assumes, uses a single `gq`. I'll correct that.

Two facts stand out. First, head 0's raw query is mostly a constant vector (mean part .551, variable part about .231), so the head's role is largely a fixed search vector. Second, attention is very sensitive to it: a 1-logit shift needs only about 6% of the query's RMS, which is a rank-1 term under 1% of the head block's norm. That's small enough to raise a new concern, because bfloat16 rounding could distort it. Entries of about 1e-4 sit right at the rounding step for typical weights around .026. So after saving I'll check the rounded tensor on the summary vectors, confirming that `Q'·m_A − Q·m_A` still reproduces `c` and that `Q'·m_P` stays nearly unchanged.

If that holds, E13 goes to a teacher-forced pass on `tf7` against pass 7. The prediction is that `fromproblem_first` rises by at least 0.5 points, likely with some loss in `fromearlier_first`. No rise there would mean wrong retrieval doesn't come from reading its own text too much.

Rounding is fine. On the summary vectors, the saved tensor keeps the direction (cos 1.000), delivers 98.5% of the planned shift at answer positions, and only 2.4% at problem positions, with the other heads untouched. The whole-tensor change is only 0.13%, which the method warns is usually too small to matter, but here attention logits are unusually sensitive to the query. The pass will show whether my 1-logit estimate is right. Notes are written and the candidate is saved, so this is the teacher-forced read against pass 7.

The per-text logprobs did move, so this tiny edit isn't inert. Now the class table against pass 7, read against the prediction I fixed earlier: `fromproblem_first` up by at least 0.5 points, with a likely cost in `fromearlier_first`. I'll also print the mean text logprob change, so this result can be compared directly with the sharpen and flatten passes.

The prediction held, at the expected cost. `fromproblem_first` rose +0.84 ± 0.27 and `othernum_first` rose +1.19 ± 0.51, while `fromearlier_first` fell -1.65 ± 0.31. This is the first attention edit that changed which source the model picks: sharpening only moved confidence, and flattening only hurt.

It looks like a trade rather than a gain, though. By hand, the number classes net about +5 correct tokens out of 12,588, and mean text logprob is flat at -0.0003. So I conclude that the balance between reading the problem and reading its own text is a real causal lever, but at this strength it nets to about zero when teacher-forced.

These scores come from reference solutions, so they can't show whether a better problem pick is worth more than a worse recall in free generation. Earlier I found that 26.6% of wrong answers miss a needed number, so the two may not count equally. Generation is the deciding test, so that's where E13 goes next.

Of the 12 passes left, 4 stay reserved for HOLDOUT. E5's failure showed that a 1-2 point DEV gain can't be trusted, so I'd count a gain of about +4 or more as support. A result near zero would mean this uniform bias only swaps one error for another. Before spending the pass, I'll record this result, confirm that E13 is saved in `cands`, and find the least-used DEV set, so the read is as clean as possible.
